summary:
Bullpen is the category to lean on today. R4's bullpen rating is running 93-68 (58%, n=161) over the last 14 days, well clear of its 46% bullpen_fatigue mark and its own 4L skid in hitting — that split matters because bullpen and trends are the two hottest levers across all four ratings right now (all sitting at 55-58% over the same window), while hitting lags at 47-49% across the board. R4 also carries the best strong-play read of the group: 61% at +18.0u over 14 days and 62% at +39.0u over 30, so when R4's delta separates from the pack, it's worth extra weight.

That's exactly what's happening in ATH @ TBR, the single strongest signal on the board — full consensus on TBR, with R4 at +2.54 clearing the other three ratings by a healthy margin. TBR as a liked team has been money all year (37-16, 70%, strong 23-9 at +19.0u), and Springs-over-Rasmussen doesn't change that home-side lean. LAD @ CIN and SDP @ COL are the other two games where all four ratings stack up big (LAD -1.35 to -1.96, SDP -1.08 to -1.61), both leaning the road/away side against the number — LAD as a liked team is 32-15 (68%) with strong plays at 80% and +24.0u, so fading Cincinnati here lines up with both the rating consensus and the team trend. MIN @ LAA is the other clean agreement spot, with LAA backed by all four ratings (+0.79 to +1.66) despite thinner separation.

Everything else on the slate — TEX, DET, MIL, NYM, HOU — is clustered under a 1.0 average delta with tight agreement across ratings, meaning low separation and lower confidence; treat these as pass/small plays rather than strong plays. Watch MIL specifically: liked at 66% season-wide with strong 67% (+14.0u), but today's -0.42 to -0.80 range against PIT is well below the signal strength seen in the TBR or LAD spots, so don't let the season-long MIL love overweight a thin daily edge.
